fix: list dual-auth providers (Anthropic, Copilot, Codex) in the Models panel (#311)

* fix: list dual-auth providers in the Models panel

Anthropic was skipped by /api/auth/all-providers as "OAuth only" and by
/api/auth/providers through a hardcoded EXCLUDED set, so a configured
Anthropic account showed up in neither provider list even though its
models were selectable in chat. The same gap hid github-copilot and
openai-codex whenever they held an API-key credential, and there was no
way to add, rotate, or remove those keys from the UI.

Replace both id-based skip lists with capability-driven listing in
lib/provider-listing.ts: a provider is offered for API-key auth when it
declares auth.apiKey.login, for OAuth when it declares auth.oauth, and
its configured/loggedIn state now follows the stored credential type so a
dual-auth provider renders exactly once. Custom models.json providers
stay excluded (models_json_key and now models_json_command too) because
the panel already renders them from models.json.

Fixes #309

* fix: keep both provider lists in sync when the auth method changes

Review follow-ups on the dual-auth listing fix:

- Refresh both provider lists after any auth change. OAuth login reloaded only
  the OAuth list and saving an API key only the API-key list, so a dual-auth
  provider stayed rendered in its old list until the panel was reopened.
- Stop the stale row from deleting the new credential. auth.json holds one
  credential per provider and `logout()` removes whichever it is, so both delete
  routes now gate on `canRemoveCredential()` and return 409 when the stored
  credential belongs to the other method. Covers a second tab the refresh above
  cannot reach.
- openai-codex is OAuth-only in the pinned SDK — drop it from the dual-auth
  examples in AGENTS.md and lib/provider-listing.ts, and correct the test stub
  that claimed otherwise. Which providers declare both is an SDK property that
  moves between releases; the docs now say so instead of naming a fixed set.

* fix: make credential deletion atomic

fix: resolve `enabledModels` glob patterns for the model selector (#310)

* fix: resolve enabledModels globs for the model selector

The model selector filtered available models by comparing enabledModels
entries as literal strings, so a pattern like "my-gateway/*" matched
nothing and every model behind it disappeared from Pi Web while pi's TUI
still listed it.

Delegate scoping to the SDK's resolveModelScopeWithDiagnostics() through
lib/model-scope.ts so globs, fuzzy patterns, and :thinkingLevel suffixes
behave exactly like pi's --models flag. Patterns that match nothing are
now reported as modelScopeWarnings instead of silently shrinking the
list, and an empty resolution still falls back to all available models.

Fixes #307

* fix: consume model-scope diagnostics and honor thinking-level pins

Review follow-ups on the enabledModels glob fix:

- Carry the `:thinkingLevel` pin through. The resolver returns
  `{ model, thinkingLevel }` for a pattern like `anthropic/*:high`, but only
  the model survived, so a new session still started at auto. `/api/models`
  now returns `thinkingLevelPins` and `useAgentSession` applies the pin of the
  model a new session starts with — the same rule as pi's buildSessionOptions.
- Give `modelScopeWarnings` a consumer: `ModelScopeWarningBanner` renders them
  above the composer, so a pattern that matched nothing is visible instead of
  silently shrinking the list.
- Drop the resolver catch-all. It could only fire when `getAvailable()` itself
  throws, which the route already handles, and it turned a real SDK fault into
  a silently unfiltered model list. The test that manufactured the throw by
  breaking an array iterator goes with it.
- Simplify `resolveVisibleModels`: take `ModelRuntime` and return pi's own
  `Model` type, removing the generic parameter, the structural runtime type and
  both `unknown` casts. `getAvailable()` is no longer called on the happy path.

* fix: apply enabled model scope at session startup

fix: gate untrusted project extensions behind project trust

Creating session services for a repository loads and executes its
project-local extensions: the SDK's resource loader imports every
enabled .pi/extensions module (running its factory) and the session then
dispatches session_start handlers. Pi Web called createAgentSessionServices
without the SDK's project-trust resolver, so merely opening an untrusted
repository — via POST /api/agent/new or GET /api/models — ran
repository-controlled code locally, with no trust prompt (#236).

Add projectTrustReloadOptions(), which returns the SDK
resourceLoaderReloadOptions only when the project has trust-requiring
resources (hasTrustRequiringProjectResources) and resolves trust from the
ProjectTrustStore shared with the pi CLI, defaulting to untrusted. The
loader's pre-trust pass keeps project extensions out until the decision is
true, so untrusted repositories no longer auto-run their code while
projects already trusted via the CLI keep working. Wire it into both
session-creation paths (startRpcSession and the models route).

Pi Web has no in-app trust prompt yet; until it does, a project is trusted
by trusting it once in the pi CLI. Ordinary projects without .pi
extensions are unaffected.

fix: allow toggling globally installed skills in PATCH /api/skills

Globally installed skills (skills add -g) live in ~/.agents/skills and
are symlinked into the agent's skills directory. PATCH /api/skills
validates the SKILL.md path with isExistingFilePathAllowed, which
resolves symlinks via realpath, so the real target lands in
~/.agents/skills — outside getAgentDir() and every other allowed root —
and the toggle returned 403 Access denied.

Add ~/.agents/skills (the SDK's canonical global skills location, which
its trust manager always treats as trusted) to the allow-list for this
check, guarded by existsSync. Listing and project-scoped installs
validate the project cwd instead and are unaffected.

fix: use a unique key for new-session RPC lock

startRpcSession coalesces concurrent callers that pass the same key onto
one shared session (in-flight lock in lib/rpc-manager.ts). The new-session
route derived that key from Date.now(), which has millisecond resolution,
so two POST /api/agent/new requests in the same millisecond received the
same AgentSessionWrapper and sessionId. Two independent chats were then
merged into a single pi session.

Use randomUUID() so the key is unique per request; the lock now only
coalesces retries of the same logical request, never two distinct ones.

fix: use streamFn key when building session title agent options

AgentOptions expects the key 'streamFn', but buildSessionTitleAgentOptions
was passing 'streamFunction' (the name of the property on the Agent instance).

The Agent constructor reads runtimeOptions.streamFn and falls back to
getDefaultStreamFn() when it is undefined. Since getDefaultStreamFn()
is never set in the pi-web server process, the temporary agent created
for title generation always threw:

  No default stream function configured. Pass streamFn explicitly
  or call setDefaultStreamFn().

This caused every POST to /api/sessions/:id/auto-name to return HTTP 500.

fix: collapse post-compaction messages when compaction drops the user prompt

When compaction fires mid-turn, pi replaces the compacted history (including
the original user prompt) with a compaction summary and the agent keeps
producing tool calls and a final answer with no user message left to anchor
the turn.

ChatWindow's message grouping only treated role==="user" as a turn anchor,
so after such a compaction every subsequent tool call and assistant reply
rendered standalone and never folded into a collapsed ProcessDetailsGroup —
the whole post-compaction tail stayed expanded even after the run ended.

Treat a compaction summary (role "custom", customType "compaction") as a
group anchor too: it renders as the compaction block, the process messages
after it fold into ProcessDetailsGroup, and the final assistant renders as
the answer. Live-tail detection now uses the last anchor (user or
compaction) instead of only the last user message, so a compaction summary
that sits after the last user message still anchors the streaming segment.

fix: prevent SSE event loss in connectEvents onerror handler

The old onerror handler unconditionally called settle() + es.close() on
every error, then manually reconnected after 1s. This created a race:

1. A recoverable network glitch triggers onerror
2. settle() resolves the Promise immediately -> handleSend proceeds to
   send the prompt
3. es.close() kills the SSE connection -> all events emitted during the
   1s reconnect window (agent_start, message_*, prompt_done, agent_end)
   are lost
4. The UI stays stuck in 'waiting for model' until reconcileAgentState
   (15s polling) recovers

The fix distinguishes between fatal errors (readyState === CLOSED, e.g.
404/500) where manual reconnect is needed, and recoverable errors
(CONNECTING) where EventSource auto-reconnects on its own. For
recoverable errors we no longer settle() or close() - the 1.5s timeout
in the Promise constructor still ensures handleSend won't hang.

fix: patch export HTML to avoid stack overflow on deep linear sessions

array) and resume (no toolNames) paths are unchanged.
